mainTopic: מילה on שבת: going back for ציצין and the source for פירש אינו חוזר, כרת for an unfinished מילה, מציצה, and the bandage
overview: The גמרא asks what the extra phrase "כל צורכי מילה" in the משנה adds. It answers with a ברייתא: while the מוהל is still busy, he may go back for any leftover shreds (ציצין). Once he has stopped (פירש), he may go back only for shreds that make the מילה invalid. The גמרא then searches for the תנא behind "פירש אינו חוזר". רבי ישמעאל בנו של רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה and רבי יוסי are each suggested and pushed aside. The final source is the רבנן who argue with רבי יוסי about the לחם הפנים: for them, even a short gap counts as a break. Next comes a ברייתא that an unfinished מילה brings כרת. After רב כהנא and רב פפא are challenged, רב אשי explains that it means a מוהל who was warned he lacked time before שבת ended, went ahead anyway, and only made a wound. The גמרא then explains the משנה's מציצה: skipping it is dangerous, like skipping the bandage and כמון. It ends with bandage recipes from אביי and רבא, and a story about רבא and the doctor's sons that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: What does the extra phrase 'all the needs of circumcision' add?
steps.stepSummary: The משנה already listed the specific parts of מילה. So the גמרא asks what the general phrase "כל צורכי מילה" comes to include.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: Since the משנה already teaches all the specific steps, what does the phrase "all the needs of circumcision" come to include?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא notices that the משנה seems to say something extra. It asks what that extra phrase is meant to add.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה already listed every step of מילה one may do on שבת. A general phrase on top of that list must be teaching something new. The גמרא wants to know what that new case is.

keyTerms.meaning: Since / after all (introduces a question based on something already known)
What does it come to include?

phrases.english: Gemara:
Since it teaches all of them (all the specific steps),
"all the needs of circumcision" comes to include what?

steps.triggerLanguage: מִכְּדֵי קָתָנֵי כּוּלְּהוּ, כׇּל צוֹרְכֵי מִילָה לְאֵתוֹיֵי מַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא on the משנה
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What extra case the general phrase "כל צורכי מילה" includes beyond the listed steps

steps.title: It includes going back to cut leftover shreds
steps.stepSummary: The phrase includes a ברייתא's rule. While the מוהל is still busy, he may go back for all shreds. After he stops, he may go back only for shreds that make the מילה invalid.
steps.simpleTranslation: It comes to include what the Rabbis taught: One who circumcises, as long as he is still busy with the circumcision, may go back for both shreds that invalidate the מילה and shreds that do not invalidate it. If he has stopped, he goes back for shreds that invalidate the מילה, but he does not go back for shreds that do not invalidate it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that "כל צורכי מילה" includes going back to cut ציצין. The answer depends on whether the מוהל is still working or has already stopped.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase teaches that even non-essential shreds may be cut on שבת, but only while the מוהל is still busy with the מילה. Once he has stopped (פירש), only shreds that are מעכבין may be cut, since without them the מצוה is not done. Shreds that do not invalidate the מילה may then no longer be cut on שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: Leftover shreds of skin from the foreskin
Invalidate / hold back (the מילה is not valid without removing them)
He withdrew / stopped (finished and stepped away)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think that after stopping one may never go back. He may still go back for shreds that invalidate the מילה, because the מצוה was never completed. The only thing forbidden is going back for non-essential shreds.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up a key idea: whether you are still in the middle of a מצוה or have already stopped changes what you may do on שבת.

phrases.english: To include that which the Rabbis taught:

phrases.aramaic: הַמָּל, כׇּל זְמַן שֶׁהוּא עוֹסֵק בַּמִּילָה —
phrases.english: One who circumcises, as long as he is engaged in the circumcision —

phrases.aramaic: חוֹזֵר בֵּין עַל הַצִּיצִין הַמְעַכְּבִין אֶת הַמִּילָה
phrases.english: returns both for the shreds that invalidate the circumcision

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין עַל הַצִּיצִין שֶׁאֵין מְעַכְּבִין אֶת הַמִּילָה.
phrases.english: and for the shreds that do not invalidate the circumcision.

phrases.aramaic: פֵּירַשׁ, עַל צִיצִין הַמְעַכְּבִין אֶת הַמִּילָה — חוֹזֵר,
phrases.english: If he withdrew: for shreds that invalidate the circumcision, he returns;

phrases.aramaic: עַל צִיצִין שֶׁאֵין מְעַכְּבִין אֶת הַמִּילָה — אֵינוֹ חוֹזֵר.
phrases.english: for shreds that do not invalidate the circumcision, he does not return.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 1
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: "כל צורכי מילה" includes going back to cut even non-essential ציצין, as long as the מוהל has not yet stopped

steps.title: Who holds that after stopping you may not go back?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which תנא is the source of the rule that once you have stopped, you may not go back for non-essential shreds.
steps.simpleTranslation: Who is the תנא who says that if he withdrew, he does not go back?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks which תנא stands behind the second half of the ברייתא. This sets up the next step, where an answer is given.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea that stopping changes the law is not obvious. One could argue that if the מצוה overrides שבת, finishing it nicely should always be allowed. So the גמרא looks for the תנא who holds this stricter view.

keyTerms.meaning: Who is the תנא (which sage taught this)?

phrases.english: Who is the tanna who holds: if he withdrew, he does not return?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the ruling cited in step 2
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The identity of the תנא who rules פירש אינו חוזר

steps.title: רבי יוחנן names רבי ישמעאל בנו של רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר בר חנה reports in the name of רבי יוחנן that this ruling follows רבי ישמעאל בנו של רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר בר חנה said in the name of רבי יוחנן: It is רבי ישמעאל, the son of רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן answers the question by naming the תנא. The proof for this comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer links the מילה rule to a specific תנא. That תנא's known view elsewhere will be brought to show that he limits what one may do on שבת to the bare minimum.

keyTerms.term: רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל בְּנוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן בְּרוֹקָה
keyTerms.meaning: A תנא, son of רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rabba bar bar Chana said that Rabbi Yochanan said:

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל בְּנוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן בְּרוֹקָה הִיא.
phrases.english: It is Rabbi Yishmael, son of Rabbi Yochanan ben Beroka.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 3
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ruling פירש אינו חוזר follows רבי ישמעאל בנו של רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה

steps.title: Proof from skinning the קרבן פסח on שבת
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא shows that רבי ישמעאל allows skinning the קרבן פסח on שבת only down to the breast, which is the minimum needed. The חכמים allow skinning the whole animal.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught: When the fourteenth of ניסן falls on שבת, a person skins the פסח only until the breast. These are the words of רבי ישמעאל, son of רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה. The חכמים say: One skins all of it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to prove רבי יוחנן's claim. It shows that רבי ישמעאל only allows the bare minimum on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Skinning until the breast is enough to remove the parts that go on the מזבח, so that is all רבי ישמעאל allows. Anything beyond the minimum is a needless שבת violation. This matches the rule that after stopping, the מוהל may not go back for non-essential shreds.

keyTerms.meaning: The 14th of ניסן, the day the קרבן פסח is brought

phrases.aramaic: דְּתַנְיָא: אַרְבָּעָה עָשָׂר שֶׁחָל לִהְיוֹת בְּשַׁבָּת —
phrases.english: As it was taught: The fourteenth (of Nisan) that falls on Shabbat —
a person flays the Paschal offering until the breast,

phrases.aramaic: דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל בְּנוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן בְּרוֹקָה.
phrases.english: these are the words of Rabbi Yishmael, son of Rabbi Yochanan ben Beroka.
And the Sages say: One flays all of it.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא: אַרְבָּעָה עָשָׂר שֶׁחָל לִהְיוֹת בְּשַׁבָּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the attribution in step 4
steps.raayaObject: That רבי ישמעאל בנו של רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה is the source of פירש אינו חוזר
steps.raayaSupportSource: ברייתא about skinning the פסח on שבת only until the חזה

steps.title: Challenge: מילה needs beautification, skinning the פסח does not
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the proof. Perhaps רבי ישמעאל limits skinning the פסח only because no beautification is needed there. By מילה, where זה אלי ואנוהו applies, he might allow going back even after stopping.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do you know this? Perhaps רבי ישמעאל said his ruling there only because there we do not need "זה אלי ואנוהו". But here, where we do need "זה אלי ואנוהו", he would agree that one may go back.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions whether the פסח case really proves anything about מילה. It points out an important difference between the two cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק "זה אלי ואנוהו" teaches that a מצוה should be done beautifully. Extra skinning adds no beauty to the קרבן פסח, but cutting even non-essential shreds makes the מילה more beautiful. So רבי ישמעאל might agree that the מוהל may go back, and the attribution to him is now in doubt.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do you know? (challenges an assumption)
He only said his ruling until here (limits a ruling to its own case)
"This is my God and I will beautify Him": do מצוות in a beautiful way

steps.confusionAlert: "הכי נמי" here does not mean רבי ישמעאל rules strictly by מילה as well. It means that by מילה he would agree with the lenient view, so one may go back. That is exactly why the proof is weakened.

phrases.english: From where (do you know this)?

phrases.aramaic: עַד כָּאן לָא קָאָמַר רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל בְּנוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן בְּרוֹקָה הָתָם —
phrases.english: Perhaps Rabbi Yishmael, son of Rabbi Yochanan ben Beroka, only stated his ruling there —
because we do not need "This is my God and I will beautify Him."
But here, where we do need "This is my God and I will beautify Him,"
here too (he would agree one may return).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the proof brought in step 5 for the attribution in step 4
steps.kashyaTarget: The attribution of פירש אינו חוזר to רבי ישמעאל based on the פסח-skinning ברייתא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The two cases differ. Extra skinning of the פסח adds no beauty, but extra cutting by מילה fulfills זה אלי ואנוהו. So רבי ישמעאל's strictness by פסח does not have to carry over to מילה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This raises the idea of beautifying a מצוה (הידור מצוה) as a reason that could allow more work on שבת. The challenge is never answered. In Step 9, רב אשי opens with "אלא", which drops the attribution to רבי ישמעאל and looks for a different תנא.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects using רבי ישמעאל's ruling about skinning the פסח as the source for פירש אינו חוזר by מילה. It does not dispute his ruling about the פסח itself.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The comparison ignores זה אלי ואנוהו. Extra skinning adds no beauty to the פסח, but cutting extra ציצין beautifies the מילה, so רבי ישמעאל might allow going back by מילה.

steps.title: The source for beautifying a מצוה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא showing that זה אלי ואנוהו teaches us to beautify מצוות. It lists examples like a beautiful סוכה, לולב, שופר, ציצית, and ספר תורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: "This is my God and I will beautify Him" means beautify yourself before Him with מצוות. Make a beautiful סוכה, a beautiful לולב, a beautiful שופר, beautiful ציצית, and a beautiful ספר תורה. Write it for His sake with beautiful ink and a beautiful quill, by a skilled scribe, and wrap it in beautiful silk.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the source for the idea of זה אלי ואנוהו, which it used in Step 6 to challenge the proof from רבי ישמעאל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 6 argued that מילה is different from skinning the פסח because מילה has a duty of beautification. This ברייתא shows that beautifying מצוות is a real Torah-based value. It also shows that the value applies even to parts of a מצוה that are not strictly required, like nice ink or silk wrapping.

keyTerms.meaning: "This is my God and I will beautify Him" (שמות ט״ו:ב׳), the source for beautifying מצוות
For His sake, with proper intent

steps.whyThisMatters: This ברייתא is the classic source for the concept known as הידור מצוה. That concept appears in many places in הלכה.

phrases.english: As it was taught in a baraita: "This is my God and I will beautify Him"
phrases.notes: The word ואנוהו is read as coming from נוי, meaning beauty.

phrases.english: Beautify yourself before Him in מצוות:
Make before Him a beautiful sukka,
and a beautiful lulav, and a beautiful shofar,
beautiful tzitzit, a beautiful Torah scroll,
and write in it for His sake with beautiful ink,
with a beautiful quill, by an expert scribe,
and wrap it in beautiful silks.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source for the concept used in the challenge of Step 6.
steps.raayaObject: That beautifying a מצוה is a real value, which is why מילה might be different from the פסח.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא expounding זה אלי ואנוהו

steps.title: Abba Shaul's different reading of the verse
steps.stepSummary: The same ברייתא continues with אבא שאול. He reads ואנוהו as "I and Him": be like God, and just as He is compassionate and merciful, so should you be.
steps.simpleTranslation: אבא שאול says: "ואנוהו" means be like Him. Just as He is gracious and merciful, so too you should be gracious and merciful.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting the ברייתא, which also contains אבא שאול's different reading of the same verse.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אבא שאול splits ואנוהו into אני והוא, meaning "I and He." That reading teaches us to imitate God's kindness, not to beautify מצוות. It is quoted only because it is part of the same ברייתא, and it is not what the גמרא is using here.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't think אבא שאול's opinion is part of the argument about מילה. The גמרא needed the first opinion in the ברייתא, about beautifying מצוות. אבא שאול just comes along with the quote.

phrases.english: Abba Shaul says: "Ve'anveihu" —
phrases.notes: He reads it as אני והוא, "I and He."

phrases.english: be similar to Him:
just as He is gracious and merciful —
so too you, be gracious and merciful.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the same ברייתא quoted in Step 7.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ואנוהו teaches us to imitate God's compassion and mercy.

steps.title: רב אשי: the ruling follows רבי יוסי
steps.stepSummary: Since the proof from רבי ישמעאל was pushed aside, רב אשי suggests a new source for the rule: רבי יוסי. He holds that witnesses may not break שבת to report a new moon that was already clearly seen.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב אשי said: Whose view is this? It is רבי יוסי's. As we learned in a משנה: Whether the new moon was clearly seen or not clearly seen, witnesses may break שבת to testify about it. רבי יוסי says: If it was clearly seen, they may not break שבת for it.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי gives a new answer to the question from Step 3: which תנא says you may not go back for non-essential shreds after stopping?
steps.deeperAnalysis: If everyone saw the new moon, other witnesses will surely testify, so traveling on שבת is unnecessary. רבי יוסי forbids it. רב אשי sees the same idea in מילה: once the needed part is done, you may not break שבת again for something extra.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather; signals a new approach after the earlier one failed
We may break שבת for it
Sanctifying the new month based on witnesses who saw the new moon

phrases.english: Rather, Rav Ashi said:
Whose is this? It is Rabbi Yosei's,
as we learned in a mishna: Whether it was clearly seen,
phrases.notes: משנה ראש השנה א:ה, about witnesses of the new moon

phrases.english: or whether it was not clearly seen —
one may desecrate Shabbat for it.
Rabbi Yosei says: If it was clearly seen —
one may not desecrate Shabbat for it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי: הָא מַנִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Step 6 knocked down the proof from רבי ישמעאל, so רב אשי offers a different תנא as the source.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא holds that once the מוהל stops, he may not return for non-essential shreds?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי יוסי, who forbids breaking שבת to testify about a new moon that was clearly seen, because the need is already covered.

steps.title: Rejecting the comparison to רבי יוסי
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב אשי's comparison. רבי יוסי is strict about the new moon because there שבת was never set aside. By מילה, שבת is already set aside, so he might allow finishing the job.
steps.simpleTranslation: How do you know? Perhaps רבי יוסי only said this there, where שבת was not set aside. But here, where שבת was set aside, he would allow it too.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רב אשי, arguing that the new-moon case may not compare to מילה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the new moon was clearly seen, these witnesses never had permission to break שבת at all. By מילה, the תורה already pushed שבת aside for this מילה, so the permission is "open." רבי יוסי might then allow going back for extra shreds, so the גמרא must look for another source, which it does in Step 11.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do you know this?
He only said his view in that specific case
שבת was given over to be set aside here
Here too, the same applies (he would permit it)

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two cases. In the new-moon case, the witnesses were never permitted to break שבת to begin with. In מילה, breaking שבת was already permitted for this מצוה. That difference is the whole point of the rejection.

phrases.english: From where do you know? Perhaps

phrases.aramaic: עַד כָּאן לָא קָאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי הָתָם,
phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei only said his view there,
where Shabbat was not given over to be set aside,
but here, where Shabbat was given over to be set aside —
indeed, he would permit it.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִמַּאי? דִּילְמָא עַד כָּאן לָא קָאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי הָתָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב אשי's proposed source from Step 9.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the proof from רבי יוסי as a source for the ruling on מילה, without disputing רבי יוסי's ruling about the new moon.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The comparison misses a key difference. By the new moon, שבת was never set aside. By מילה, שבת was already set aside, so finishing the מצוה might still be allowed.

steps.title: The נהרדעי offer a new source
steps.stepSummary: The נהרדעי say the rule about not going back to the מילה follows the רבנן who argue with רבי יוסי.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the Sages of נהרדעא say: this ruling follows the רבנן who argue with רבי יוסי.
steps.whatsHappening: The earlier attempts to find a source were rejected, so the נהרדעי suggest a different one. This line sets up the next move: the גמרא is about to quote the משנה where רבי יוסי and the רבנן argue.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אשי tried to base the rule on רבי יוסי, but that comparison was pushed aside. Now the source is flipped to the רבנן who argue with רבי יוסי. They are about to be shown as holding that even a short break counts as a real stop.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather (this drops the previous idea and brings a new one)
The Sages of the city of נהרדעא

phrases.english: Rather, the Sages of Neharde'a say:

phrases.aramaic: רַבָּנַן דִּפְלִיגִי עֲלֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי הִיא.
phrases.english: It is the Rabbis who disagree with Rabbi Yosei.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces רב אשי's source, which was rejected in step 10
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The source for the rule is the רבנן who argue with רבי יוסי

steps.title: The showbread loaves must overlap on the table
steps.stepSummary: The משנה describes how the old and new לחם הפנים were switched so that the table was never empty, because the פסוק says 'תמיד'.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned in a משנה: Four כהנים go in. Two hold the two rows of bread, and two hold the two bowls of לבונה. Four more go in ahead of them: two to take the two old rows, and two to take the two old bowls. The ones bringing in stand in the north, facing south. The ones taking out stand in the south, facing north. These slide the old bread off, and these put the new bread on, so one handbreadth of new bread sits next to one handbreadth of old bread. This is because the פסוק says 'before Me always.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the משנה about changing the לחם הפנים each שבת. This is the opinion of the רבנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to the רבנן, the new bread had to touch the table before the old bread was fully off, so there was never even one moment with no bread. This shows they think even a tiny gap breaks the 'תמיד'. In the same way, a short pause in the מילה counts as a real stop.

keyTerms.meaning: Rows of bread (the לחם הפנים was set in two rows of six)

steps.confusionAlert: This משנה is not about מילה at all. It is quoted only to show how the רבנן look at a short break in a מצוה.

phrases.english: As we learned in a mishna:
Four priests would enter:
two with the two rows of bread in their hands,
and two with the two bowls of frankincense in their hands.
And four would go ahead of them:
two to take the two old rows,
and two to take the two old bowls.
Those bringing in stand in the north, facing south,
and those taking out stand in the south, facing north.
These slide the old bread off, and these place the new,

phrases.aramaic: טִפְחוֹ שֶׁל זֶה בְּצַד טִפְחוֹ שֶׁל זֶה,
phrases.english: the handbreadth of this one alongside the handbreadth of that one,
because it says: 'Before Me always.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the משנה behind the נהרדעי's claim
steps.raayaObject: The רבנן view that even a moment's gap counts as a break

steps.title: רבי יוסי says a short gap is fine
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי holds that even if the old bread is fully removed first and the new bread is placed afterward, it still counts as 'תמיד'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי says: even if these take the old bread off, and only then these put the new bread on, this too counts as 'always.'
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה brings רבי יוסי's opposing view. This completes the picture of the argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יוסי, a short gap does not break continuity. So the רבנן, who argue with him, must hold that a short gap does break it. That is why the rule that a מוהל who stopped cannot go back fits the רבנן.
steps.whatToRemember: The rule that you cannot go back after stopping the מילה fits the רבנן, for whom any pause counts as a real stop. It does not fit רבי יוסי.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei says:
Even if these first take off the old bread
and then these place the new bread,
this too counts as 'always.'

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר: אֲפִילּוּ אֵלּוּ נוֹטְלִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing view in the same משנה, which shows what the רבנן hold
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A short gap does not break 'תמיד'

steps.title: A circumcision must be finished properly
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that the מילה must be cut fully, and if it was not, someone is punished with כרת.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Sages taught: we finish cutting the מילה fully. If it was not finished, the person is punished with כרת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא about finishing a מילה properly. This sets up the question in the next step: who gets the כרת?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says an unfinished מילה is very serious. However, it does not say whose fault it is or who is punished.

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
We finish cutting the circumcision fully,
and if he did not finish it, he is punished with karet.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic connected to finishing a מילה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An unfinished מילה brings a punishment of כרת

steps.title: Who is punished?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks who the ברייתא means is punished with כרת.
steps.simpleTranslation: Who is it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a simple clarifying question: who exactly gets the כרת?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא did not say who is punished. It could be the מוהל, or it could be the person being circumcised.

phrases.english: Who is it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the ברייתא in step 14
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Who is the one punished with כרת

steps.title: רב כהנא: the circumciser
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא says the ברייתא means the מוהל.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב כהנא said: the craftsman, meaning the מוהל.
steps.whatsHappening: רב כהנא answers that the one punished is the מוהל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea is that on שבת the מוהל wounded the baby without completing the מצוה. So his cutting turns into a plain חילול שבת, which is punished with כרת.

phrases.english: Rav Kahana said: The craftsman.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 15
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The מוהל, for cutting on שבת without finishing

steps.title: רב פפא: the מוהל did half a מצוה
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא objects that the מוהל can say he did half the מצוה and others should finish it, so why should he get כרת?
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא objects: the מוהל can tell them, 'I did half the מצוה. You also do half the מצוה!'
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא attacks רב כהנא's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The מוהל was busy doing a real מצוה when he cut. His cutting is not a sin just because someone else must finish. So it makes no sense to punish him with כרת.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa strongly objects:
Let the craftsman say to them:
'I did half the מצוה,
you [also] do half the מצוה!'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב כהנא's answer
steps.kashyaTarget: רב כהנא's claim that the מוהל gets כרת
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The מוהל did a valid part of the מצוה and can leave the rest to others, so he did nothing wrong

steps.title: רב פפא: the adult being circumcised
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא says the ברייתא means an adult whose own מילה was left unfinished.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב פפא said: it means an adult.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא gives his own answer: the one punished with כרת is a grown man whose מילה was not finished.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This ברייתא is not about שבת at all. It is about the general מצוה of מילה. An adult whose cut was left unfinished still counts as not circumcised, so he carries the כרת of an ערל.
steps.whatToRemember: This is only רב פפא's reading: the כרת falls on an adult whose own מילה was left unfinished, because a partial מילה does not count. רב אשי rejects this reading in Step 19 and gives the final answer in Step 20.

phrases.english: Rather, Rav Pappa said: An adult.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces רב כהנא's reading after the challenge
steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-identifying the subject of the ברייתא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The מוהל is punished for cutting on שבת without finishing
steps.terutzMaskana: An adult whose own מילה is unfinished is the one with כרת

steps.title: רב אשי: An adult's punishment is already written in the תורה
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי challenges רב פפא: the תורה already says plainly that an uncircumcised adult gets כרת, so the ברייתא would be teaching nothing new.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי objected: About an adult it is written clearly, 'And an uncircumcised male who will not be circumcised.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי attacks רב פפא's answer from Step 18. He says the ברייתא cannot be about an adult, because the תורה already says so openly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A ברייתא is expected to teach something we did not already know. The פסוק in בראשית already gives כרת to an adult who stays uncircumcised. So if the ברייתא only meant an adult, it would just be repeating the פסוק.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi objected to it:
About an adult it is written explicitly:
phrases.notes: So the ברייתא would add nothing new.

phrases.english: 'And an uncircumcised male who will not be circumcised' (Genesis 17:14).
phrases.notes: The פסוק ends that this soul will be cut off, which is כרת.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב פפא's explanation from Step 18.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב פפא's claim that the ברייתא refers to an adult whose own מילה was left unfinished.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: That explanation makes the ברייתא repeat an explicit פסוק, and a ברייתא should not teach something already stated in the תורה.

steps.title: רב אשי: It is the circumciser who started too late
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי says the ברייתא is about the מוהל after all. It is a special case where he insisted he could finish before the end of שבת, did not finish, and so only made a wound on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב אשי said: It really is about the מוהל. The case is where he came at twilight at the edge of שבת. People told him, 'You won't manage to finish,' and he said, 'I will manage.' He did it and did not manage. It turns out he only made a wound, and he is punished with כרת.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי goes back to רב כהנא's idea that the ברייתא means the מוהל. He answers רב פפא's question by describing one specific case where the מוהל really is to blame.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a מוהל can say he did part of the מצוה and someone else can finish, which was רב פפא's objection in Step 17. Here, though, time was running out and nobody else could finish within the time allowed. Since he was warned and went ahead anyway, his cut was not a מצוה at all. It was just a wound made on שבת, which is a real חילול שבת deserving כרת.

keyTerms.meaning: Really, actually (returning to an earlier idea)
Twilight, the uncertain time between day and night
I will manage (to finish in time)

steps.confusionAlert: The כרת here is not for leaving the מצוה unfinished in general. It is for breaking שבת: since no מצוה was completed, his cut was only a forbidden wound made on שבת.
steps.whatToRemember: Final answer: the ברייתא's כרת is on a מוהל who was warned that he lacked time, went ahead, and failed. His act became just a wound on שבת.

phrases.english: Rather, Rav Ashi said:
Actually, it is the professional circumciser,
and the case is where he came at twilight at the edge of Shabbat,
and they told him: 'You will not manage to finish in time,'
and he told them: 'I will manage,'
and he did it and did not manage,
and it turns out that he only made a wound,
phrases.notes: There was no מצוה, only a forbidden cut.

phrases.english: and he is punished with karet.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי: לְעוֹלָם אוּמָּן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After rejecting the adult explanation in Step 19, רב אשי gives a new reading.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case to a specific scenario
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A מוהל can always leave the job for others to finish, so he should never get כרת.
steps.terutzMaskana: When time ran out and he had been warned, no one else could finish, so his cut was only a wound on שבת and he gets כרת.

steps.title: רב פפא: A circumciser who skips sucking is a danger
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's rule of מציצה. רב פפא says a מוהל who does not suck the blood endangers the baby and is removed from his job.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'We suck the blood.' רב פפא said: A מוהל who does not suck the blood is a danger, and we remove him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic by quoting the next words of the משנה, 'מוצצין', about sucking the blood. רב פפא then gives a practical rule about this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב פפא makes מציצה a matter of the baby's safety, not just a custom. Because skipping it puts the child at risk, a מוהל who does not do it may not keep working as a מוהל.

keyTerms.meaning: We suck (the blood after the cut)
Etc., the quote continues in the משנה

steps.whyThisMatters: This statement is the source for treating מציצה as a required part of a safe ברית מילה.

phrases.english: 'We suck the blood,' etc.
Rav Pappa said:
A circumciser who does not suck the blood —
it is a danger, and we remove him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to a new line of the משנה, about מציצה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Not doing מציצה endangers the baby, so a מוהל who skips it is removed.

steps.title: Isn't that obvious, since we break שבת for it?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רב פפא needed to say this. We already know מציצה is a matter of danger, because the משנה lets us break שבת for it.
steps.simpleTranslation: That is obvious! Since we break שבת for it, it must be a matter of danger!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב פפא's statement as unnecessary. The משנה already shows the danger by allowing מציצה on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We only break שבת for something serious like danger to life. So if the משנה allows מציצה on שבת, it seems clear that skipping it is dangerous. That would make רב פפא's statement add nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: It is obvious (so why say it?)

phrases.english: It is obvious!
Since we break Shabbat for it,
it must be a danger!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions whether רב פפא's statement in Step 21 is needed.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב פפא's statement that skipping מציצה is a danger.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה already allows מציצה on שבת, which shows it is a matter of danger, so רב פפא adds nothing.

steps.title: The blood is still attached, so sucking it really breaks שבת
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers: we might have thought the blood is just sitting there, so sucking it is not a real מלאכה. The lesson is that the blood is still attached, so only danger can allow it.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said that this blood is just stored up in place. So it teaches us that it is attached.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why רב פפא's statement is not obvious. Without it, we could have found a different reason why מציצה is allowed on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the blood were only pooled in place, drawing it out might not count as a forbidden מלאכה at all, and the משנה would allow it even without danger. רב פפא teaches that the blood is still attached to the body, so drawing it out is truly forbidden on שבת. It is allowed only because of danger.

keyTerms.meaning: It is stored up, just sitting in place
It is attached (still connected to the body)

phrases.english: You might have said
that this blood is stored up in place,
phrases.notes: So sucking it would not be a real מלאכה.

phrases.english: so it teaches us
that it is attached.
phrases.notes: Drawing it out is a real איסור, allowed only because of danger.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַהוּ דְתֵימָא הַאי דָּם מִיפְקָד פְּקִיד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the פשיטא question from Step 22.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Showing another possible reason (מהו דתימא / קא משמע לן)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The blood is only pooled, so sucking it is not a forbidden מלאכה, and the משנה's permission proves nothing about danger.
steps.terutzMaskana: The blood is attached, so sucking it is a real איסור that only danger can allow.

steps.title: Sucking is like the bandage and cumin: skipping it is dangerous
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא supports the danger point from the משנה itself. מציצה is listed together with the bandage and כמון, which are done because skipping them is dangerous, so the same is true of מציצה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And it is like the bandage and cumin: just as with the bandage and cumin, not doing it is a danger, so too here, not doing it is a danger.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up רב פפא by pointing to the order of the משנה. It finishes the discussion of מציצה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה lists מציצה next to putting on a bandage and כמון. Those are clearly done to protect the baby. Since מציצה is grouped with them, it is also a safety step, and skipping it is dangerous.

keyTerms.meaning: A bandage or compress put on the wound
Cumin, used as a healing powder

steps.whatToRemember: מציצה is a safety measure like the bandage and כמון. That is why it overrides שבת, and why a מוהל who skips it is removed.

phrases.english: And it is like the bandage and cumin:
phrases.notes: Both are listed in the same משנה.

phrases.english: Just as with the bandage and cumin,
when one does not do it, it is a danger,
so too here as well,
when one does not do it, it is a danger.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds support from the משנה's list to the danger point in Steps 21 and 23.
steps.raayaObject: That skipping מציצה is a danger.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה groups מציצה with the bandage and כמון, which are clearly done for safety.

steps.title: אביי's nurse gives a bandage recipe
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's rule that we put a bandage on the מילה wound. אביי reports his nurse's recipe for a bandage good for all wounds: seven parts fat and one part wax.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: "And we put a bandage on it." אביי said: My nurse told me that a bandage for all wounds is made of seven parts fat and one part wax.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next item in the משנה, the bandage. אביי explains how to make a good one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This works the same way as the earlier discussion of מציצה: the גמרא picks up one phrase from the משנה and adds practical detail. Here the detail is medical. It tells us what the bandage is actually made of, and the recipe is meant to heal every kind of wound.

keyTerms.meaning: A bandage or medicated dressing placed on a wound
Literally 'mother'; here it means אביי's nurse, who raised him

steps.confusionAlert: When אביי says "אם" (mother), he means the nurse who raised him, not his birth mother. אביי often quotes her remedies.

phrases.english: And we place a bandage on it (the wound).
Abaye said: My nurse told me:
A bandage for all wounds is:
seven parts fat and one part wax.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְנוֹתְנִין עָלֶיהָ אִיסְפְּלָנִית. אָמַר אַבָּיֵי, אֲמַרָה לִי אֵם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After finishing מציצה, the גמרא moves on to the next item listed in the משנה, the bandage.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A healing bandage for any wound is made of seven parts fat and one part wax.

steps.title: רבא gives a different bandage recipe
steps.stepSummary: רבא says the bandage should be made from wax and tree sap.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: The bandage is made of wax and tree sap.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא offers his own recipe for the bandage, which differs from אביי's.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both recipes use wax. אביי adds fat, while רבא adds tree sap. This is a practical difference in medical tradition, not a debate about what the הלכה allows on שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: Sap or resin from a tree

phrases.english: Rava said: wax and tree sap.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second recipe that differs from אביי's.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The bandage is made of wax and tree sap.

steps.title: The doctor's sons tear their clothes when רבא teaches the cure publicly
steps.stepSummary: רבא taught the bandage recipe in public in מחוזא. The sons of מניומי the doctor tore their clothes because their secret medical knowledge was now known to everyone.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא taught this in public in מחוזא. The sons of מניומי the doctor tore their clothes.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a short story. רבא's public teaching upset the local doctor's family, who feared losing their income.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The doctors made a living from cures that ordinary people did not know. Once רבא taught the recipe openly, people could make the bandage themselves. Tearing clothes is a sign of great distress, like mourning. This sets up רבא's response in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: He taught it publicly, in a lecture
מחוזא, the city where רבא lived and taught

phrases.english: Rava taught it publicly in Mechoza,
and the sons of Manyomei the doctor tore their clothes.
phrases.notes: They were upset that their trade secret was now public.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tells what happened when רבא taught his recipe in public.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The public teaching of the cure caused distress to the professional doctors.

steps.title: רבא comforts them by saving one remedy, quoting שמואל
steps.stepSummary: רבא tells the doctor's sons that he left one remedy for them. He then begins quoting שמואל: a person who washes his face and does not dry it well will get a skin problem. This passage ends in the middle of this sentence.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to them: I left you one cure. For שמואל said: Someone who washes his face and does not dry it well will develop...
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the doctors' distress. He tells them he kept one remedy secret so they can still earn from it. He starts to quote שמואל about it, and the text continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא shows concern for the doctors' livelihood. He did not reveal every cure he knew. The remedy he held back connects to שמואל's warning about not drying one's face, which causes a skin condition. The name of the condition and its cure come on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: Will develop, literally 'will be tied to him' (a skin condition)

steps.confusionAlert: This passage stops in the middle of שמואל's sentence. The words נקטרו ליה lead into the name of the skin condition, which comes in the next part of the text.

phrases.english: He said to them: I left you one (cure).
For Shmuel said:
Someone who washes his face
and does not dry it well
will develop
phrases.notes: The sentence continues on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to the doctor's sons' distress from step 27.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבא held back one remedy, connected to שמואל's teaching about not drying one's face, so the doctors could still profit from it.
